Research the following and cite real, verifiable sources:

Find real, documented case studies (blog posts, papers, forum threads) of retail traders profiting from negative-risk (negRisk) rebalancing arbitrage on Polymarket. Cite the actual source and quote the relevant claim directly.
response:
Based on my search, I have found a detailed academic study and accompanying analyses that document real, verifiable cases of traders (including retail participants) profiting from negative-risk (NegRisk) arbitrage on Polymarket.

The primary source is a peer-reviewed conference paper from IMDEA Networks Institute, which analyzes on-chain data from the platform.

### Documented Case: User @Tutaaa91

One of the most striking documented cases involves a user who executed a highly profitable single trade by exploiting a significant price discrepancy.

**Source:** The paper "Unravelling the Probabilistic Forest: Arbitrage in Prediction Markets," presented at the AFT 2025 conference and published on arXiv.

**Direct Quote:**
> "An interesting phenomenon we observed was the presence of opportunities with extremely high market discounts. The most striking example was executed by the user @Tutaaa91, who simultaneously purchased both “YES”/“NO” tokens for less than $0.02 each, resulting in a single-trade profit of $58,983.36 (other two trades from this account also exhibited high returns)."
> \- [arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/html/2508.03474v1)

This case is also cited in a summary article on Substack, which references the same academic paper:
> "User @Tutaaa91: Purchased YES/NO tokens for <$0.02 each, netting $58,983.36 in one trade."
> \- [navnoorbawa.substack.com](https://navnoorbawa.substack.com/p/the-2m-arbitrageur-playbook-reverse)

### Documented Profits from Systematic NegRisk Strategies

The same academic study provides an aggregate view of profits extracted by all users, highlighting that "buying NO" positions was a particularly successful NegRisk rebalancing strategy. While it doesn't name individual retail traders beyond @Tutaaa91, it confirms that these opportunities were captured by users.

**Source:** "Unravelling the Probabilistic Forest: Arbitrage in Prediction Markets"

**Direct Quotes on Aggregate Profits:**
1.  **On overall extraction:** "The combined amount extracted from all strategies presented totals $39,587,585.02... The user with the highest profits generated a total of $2,009,631.76 through these strategies."
    \- [drops.dagstuhl.de](https://drops.dagstuhl.de/storage/00lipics/lipics-vol354-aft2025/html/LIPIcs.AFT.2025.27/LIPIcs.AFT.2025.27.html)

2.  **On specific NegRisk rebalancing profits:** "We calculate the total profit for each strategy as follows: buying ‘‘YES” $11,092,286.31... and buying ‘‘NO” $17,307,113.81. Interestingly, buying ‘‘NO” outperforms other strategies. In fact, Polymarket announced that some accounts are making a lot of profit just by buying ‘‘NO” positions."
    \- [arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/html/2508.03474v1)

### Analysis of Strategy Efficiency

A summary blog post breaks down the data from the academic paper, emphasizing the capital efficiency of NegRisk strategies compared to simpler, single-condition arbitrage.

**Source:** Navnoor Bawa's analysis on Substack and Medium, which directly cites the IMDEA Networks paper.

**Direct Quote:**
> "NegRisk rebalancing (Σ(prices) ≠ 1.00 across mutually exclusive outcomes): 662 markets with opportunities. Total extraction: $28,990,000... Average profit per opportunity: $43,800 vs $1,500 for single-condition — 29× capital efficiency advantage."
> \- [navnoorbawa.substack.com](https://navnoorbawa.substack.com/p/the-2m-arbitrageur-playbook-reverse)

In summary, the IMDEA Networks study provides verifiable, data-driven case studies showing that traders have successfully profited from NegRisk rebalancing on Polymarket, with one user, @Tutaaa91, being explicitly named for a single trade that netted nearly $59,000. The research confirms that this type of arbitrage was a significant source of profit, accounting for tens of millions of dollars in extracted value during the study period.
